name: MAX6675 K-type thermocouple amplifier
description: Maxim/Analog Devices cold-junction-compensated K-type thermocouple-to-digital converter: reads 0 to +1023.75 °C in 0.25 °C steps over a read-only SPI interface (SO, SCK, CS), with open-thermocouple detection. Runs on 3.0–5.5 V. Sold as: MAX6675 K-type thermocouple module (common red clone breakout, 5-pin header GND VCC SCK CS SO, screw terminal for the probe) with K-type probe.
eli5: Lets your board read very hot temperatures, like an oven or a soldering iron, from a metal thermocouple probe.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply, 3.0–5.5 V (use 3.3 V with an ESP32 or Pico so SO stays at 3.3 V logic)

pins.name: SCK
pins.description: Serial clock input, up to 4.3 MHz

pins.name: CS
pins.description: Chip select, active low. Low stops a conversion and starts the read; high starts a new conversion

pins.name: SO
pins.description: Serial data out (16 bits, MSB first) to the board's MISO

supplierQuery: MAX6675 K-type thermocouple module with probe
buildNotes: Power the module from 3.3 V when using an ESP32 or Pico: SO swings to VCC, and 5 V on a GPIO can damage the board.
The chip only sends data (no MOSI). Read 16 bits with CS low in SPI mode 0, at most 4.3 MHz.
Taking CS low stops the conversion in progress; a new one starts when CS goes high and takes up to 0.22 s. Do not read faster than about 4 times a second or the reading never updates.
Temperature = bits D14..D3 × 0.25 °C. Bit D2 = 1 means the probe is not connected; bit D15 and D1 are always 0.
Keep the probe polarity right (red/+ and blue or yellow/− vary by vendor): a reversed probe reads down when it heats up.
Use only a K-type thermocouple; the module reads 0 °C and up, not below freezing.

driver.code:
# MAX6675 cold-junction-compensated K-type thermocouple-to-digital converter, MicroPython driver.
# Written from the Maxim/Analog Devices MAX6675 datasheet (19-2235):
#  - CS low stops any conversion and puts D15 on SO; 16 clocks read D15..D0 MSB first.
#  - CS high starts a new conversion, which takes up to 0.22 s.
#  - D15 = dummy sign bit (always 0), D14..D3 = 12-bit temperature, 0.25 degC per LSB,
#    D2 = 1 when the thermocouple input is open, D1 = device ID (always 0), D0 = three-state.
#  - SCK up to 4.3 MHz; SO changes after SCK falls, so read in SPI mode 0.
from machine import Pin
import time

CONVERSION_MS = 220  # datasheet maximum conversion time


class MAX6675:
    def __init__(self, spi, cs):
        """spi: a machine.SPI (mode 0, <= 4.3 MHz) with SO on MISO; cs: GPIO number or Pin."""
        self.spi = spi
        self.cs = cs if isinstance(cs, Pin) else Pin(cs, Pin.OUT, value=1)
        self.cs.value(1)  # CS high starts the first conversion (pass a Pin already set to Pin.OUT)
        self._started = time.ticks_ms()

    def read_raw(self):
        """Return the 16-bit word D15..D0, waiting for a conversion to finish first."""
        wait = CONVERSION_MS - time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), self._started)
        if wait > 0:
            time.sleep_ms(wait)
        self.cs.value(0)
        b = self.spi.read(2)
        self.cs.value(1)  # start the next conversion
        self._started = time.ticks_ms()
        return (b[0] << 8) | b[1]

    def read(self):
        """Thermocouple temperature in degC (0 to 1023.75, 0.25 degC steps)."""
        raw = self.read_raw()
        if raw & 0x8002:
            # D15 and D1 are always 0 on a working MAX6675; 1s mean SO is floating.
            raise OSError('MAX6675 not responding: check SO, SCK, CS and power')
        if raw & 0x0004:
            raise OSError('thermocouple open: check the probe on T+ / T-')
        return ((raw >> 3) & 0x0FFF) * 0.25

example.code:
from machine import Pin, SPI
import sys, time
from max6675 import MAX6675

# Pico: SPI0 reaches GP16/GP18; ESP32: any pins via SPI(1). SO goes to MISO, MOSI is not used.
spi = SPI(0 if sys.platform == 'rp2' else 1, baudrate=1000000, polarity=0, phase=0, sck=Pin({SCK}), miso=Pin({SO}))
tc = MAX6675(spi, {CS})
while True:
    try:
        print('T=%.2fC' % tc.read())
    except OSError as e:
        print(e)
    time.sleep_ms(500)
